items.title: Iran says ambassador will stay in Beirut despite Lebanon's expulsion order

featured_image.name: Iran Says Envoy Will Remain in Beirut Despite Lebanon Order to ...

items.description:
Iran on Monday openly refused to comply with Lebanon's order to expel its ambassador, declaring that the envoy would remain in Beirut and continue his duties — a direct challenge to the Lebanese government's authority that has deepened a diplomatic crisis at the heart of the broader regional conflict between Israel and Hezbollah.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei confirmed at a news conference that Ambassador Mohammad Reza Shibani had no plans to leave. "Our embassy is open and our ambassador continues his work in Beirut and remains present," Baghaei said, according to Iran International. The statement came one day after a March 29 deadline set by Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raggi for Shibani to depart the country.[1][2][3]

items.title: NYU closes Abu Dhabi campus after Iran threatens US universities

featured_image.name: Overview - NYU Abu Dhabi

items.description:
New York University has temporarily shut down its Abu Dhabi campus after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared American university outposts in the Middle East "legitimate targets" for retaliation, marking a sharp escalation that extends the ongoing conflict into the realm of civilian academic institutions.

The closure, announced on Monday, suspends physical access to the campus for all students, faculty, and staff, with classes continuing remotely, according to NYU's student newspaper, Washington Square News. The university said the decision was made "out of an abundance of caution" following the IRGC's threat on Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Kuwaiti oil tanker hit by projectile near Dubai port

featured_image.name: Kuwait says its giant crude oil tanker Al-Salmi was directly targeted by an  Iranian attack while anchored in the anchorage area of Dubai Port, UAE. The  tanker was fully loaded at the

items.description:
A fully loaded Kuwaiti crude oil tanker was struck by a projectile while anchored near Dubai port early on Tuesday, March 31, sparking a fire onboard and raising fears of an oil spill in the Persian Gulf, according to Kuwait's state news agency and a British maritime monitoring authority.

Kuwait Petroleum Corporation said the very large crude carrier Al Salmi was "directly targeted in what it described as an Iranian attack while in the anchorage area of Dubai Port in the United Arab Emirates," the state news agency KUNA reported, as cited by Reuters. The corporation warned of a possible oil spill in surrounding waters, adding that the tanker was fully loaded at the time of the strike. No crew casualties were reported, and emergency response and firefighting teams were mobilized to contain the situation.[1]

items.title: Iran's parliament approves plan to toll ships in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline 2nd time for Iran to open the Strait of ...

items.description: Iran's parliamentary security commission on Monday approved a plan to impose tolls on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing a fee system that has been operating on an ad hoc basis since the outbreak of war in late February and setting up a likely flashpoint in ongoing peace negotiations with the United States.

items.title: Zelensky says Russia exploiting Iran war to fund its fight against Ukraine

featured_image.name: Russia took satellite images of U.S. air base before Iranian attack ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Monday that a prolonged war in Iran is delivering outsized benefits to Russia while undermining Ukraine's security, telling Axios in an exclusive interview that Moscow is exploiting the Middle East conflict to boost its war economy and erode Western support for Kyiv.[1]

"I am sure Russia wants long war. They have benefits: The U.S. is focusing on the Middle East and may decrease military help to Ukraine. Sanctions are partially lifted. I see only benefits for Russia from the war with Iran continuing," Zelensky said over Zoom after returning from a tour of Middle Eastern capitals.[1]

items.title: Trump threatens to destroy Iran's energy infrastructure if no deal reached

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Trump's approval hits new 36% low as fuel prices surge amid Iran  war, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds | Reuters

items.description:
President Trump on Monday threatened to "completely obliterate" Iran's electric generating plants, oil wells, and Kharg Island — and possibly its desalination plants — if a peace deal is not reached "shortly" and the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened, dramatically escalating his rhetoric as the war entered its 31st day.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that "The United States of America is in serious discussions with A NEW, AND MORE REASONABLE, REGIME to end our Military Operations in Iran," claiming "great progress" had been made. But he warned that absent a deal, "we will conclude our lovely 'stay' in Iran by blowing up and completely obliterating all of their Electric Generating Plants, Oil Wells and Kharg Island (and possibly all desalinization plants!), which we have purposefully not yet 'touched'".[1][2][3]

items.title: Netanyahu says Iran war is 'beyond the halfway point'

featured_image.name: Netanyahu says Iran's uranium enrichment abilities destroyed

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Monday that the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran has passed its midway mark, with the current focus shifting to securing or removing Iran's remaining stockpile of enriched uranium. The remarks came during an exclusive sit-down interview with Newsmax CEO Chris Ruddy in Jerusalem — Netanyahu's first in-depth interview since the war began on February 28.[1][2]

Netanyahu described the mission as "beyond the halfway point" but declined to put a specific timeline on the conflict's conclusion, saying there is still "a lot more to do". He expressed confidence in the trajectory of the campaign, framing Iran as emerging weaker while the U.S.-Israel alliance grows stronger.[3]

items.title: Tanker struck near Dubai as Gulf attacks mount

featured_image.name: Crude Oil Prices Jump on Fears of a Wider Conflict in the Middle East

items.description: An unknown projectile struck a tanker approximately 31 nautical miles northwest of Dubai on Monday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, adding to a relentless series of attacks on commercial shipping that has upended global energy markets since the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran erupted on February 28.

items.title: Iran denies direct talks with U.S. as Trump claims deal is close

featured_image.name: Trump holds situation room meeting on Iran nuclear deal negotiations

items.description: President Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday that U.S.-Iran negotiations were going "extremely well" through both direct and indirect channels, claiming a deal to end the war could come soon. But Iran flatly denied any direct engagement, and the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee accused Trump of fabricating the talks to stabilize rattled financial markets.[1][2]

items.title: Study: Earth can sustain only 2.5 billion people

featured_image.name: 3D Globe of World Population Density

items.description: The Earth can no longer sustain its current human population, according to a study published Monday in Environmental Research Letters by an international team of researchers. The paper concludes that the planet's sustainable carrying capacity is roughly 2.5 billion people — less than a third of today's 8.3 billion — and that decades of fossil fuel dependence have masked the true scale of ecological overshoot.[1][2]

items.title: White House says U.S. is 'on track' in Iran war as Strait of Hormuz remains closed

featured_image.name: Iran says will attack any ship trying to pass through Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said Monday that the United States is "on track" to meet the goals of Operation Epic Fury on its 30th day, reiterating a set of military objectives that notably does not include reopening the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20 percent of the world's oil normally flows.[1][2]

"The president, commander-in-chief, and the Pentagon has always stated four to six weeks estimated timeline," Leavitt told reporters. "We're on Day 30 today. So, you do the math on how much longer the Pentagon needs to fully achieve the objectives."[2]

items.title: Ukraine says Russia recruited 27,000 from 135 countries

featured_image.name: Russia increases recruitment of foreign fighters through ...

items.description: Ukraine's military intelligence has identified 27,407 nationals from 135 countries recruited into Russia's armed forces, according to data released on March 30. The figures underscore what the European Parliament has classified as human trafficking, as Moscow turns to deceptive recruitment across Africa, Cuba, and Central Asia to replenish its frontline forces more than four years into its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.[1][2]

items.title: Rubio chastises NATO allies for inaction during Iran war

featured_image.name: Rubio tells Al Jazeera that Strait of Hormuz to reopen 'one way or ...

items.description:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio used an exclusive Al Jazeera interview published Monday to chastise NATO allies for their inaction during the U.S.-led war in Iran, questioning "what is in it for the United States" if the alliance fails to support American military objectives. The remarks echo language Rubio first used in January before a Senate committee, when he declared that "without the U.S., there is no NATO", a line that has become a recurring theme as the conflict tests transatlantic solidarity.[1][2][3]

The wide-ranging interview, segments of which Al Jazeera released throughout the day, saw Rubio outline U.S. demands for Iran and assert that the Strait of Hormuz would "reopen one way or another" once the war concludes. He warned Tehran of "serious repercussions" if it continued blocking the waterway and said President Trump "always prefers diplomacy," noting that indirect talks between the two sides are underway through intermediaries.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Trump floats asking Arab states to help pay for Iran war

featured_image.name: Trump Seems to Embrace 'Regime Change' in Iran - TIME

items.description:
President Donald Trump is interested in calling on Arab countries to help cover the costs of the war in Iran, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt indicated during a briefing on Monday, as the month-old conflict's price tag continues to climb and diplomatic efforts intensify across the region.[1][2][3]

The remarks come as the Pentagon has already estimated the war's first six days alone cost more than $11.3 billion, with independent analysts projecting total spending may have exceeded $25 billion by late March. Trump has previously called on Middle Eastern allies — including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait — to take on greater responsibility in the conflict, including policing the Strait of Hormuz.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Israel Knesset passes death penalty law for Palestinians

featured_image.name: Israel Knesset set to vote on death penalty law for ...

items.description:
Israel's parliament voted on Monday to impose the death penalty on Palestinians in the West Bank convicted of deadly attacks against Israelis, a move that drew immediate international condemnation and is expected to face a swift legal challenge before the country's Supreme Court.

The Knesset passed the measure 62–48 after nearly twelve hours of debate, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu personally voting in favor in the final moments. The law represents a major victory for far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, whose Otzma Yehudit party has long championed the legislation.[1]

items.title: NATO intercepts fourth Iranian missile over Turkey

featured_image.name: NATO defences destroy missile fired from Iran over Mediterranean

items.description:
NATO air and missile defense systems deployed in the Eastern Mediterranean intercepted a fourth Iranian ballistic missile entering Turkish airspace on Monday, Turkey's Defense Ministry reported, extending a pattern of alarming incursions that has tested the alliance's readiness and complicated Ankara's dual role as both a NATO member and diplomatic intermediary in the wider conflict.[1]

The ministry stated that "all necessary measures are being taken decisively and without hesitation against any threat directed at our country's territory and airspace," language consistent with its prior statements on similar incidents. It did not disclose the missile's type, trajectory, or intended target.[2]

items.title: 3 Indonesian UNIFIL peacekeepers killed in Lebanon in 24 hours

featured_image.name: One UNIFIL peacekeeper killed, another wounded in southern ...

items.description: Three Indonesian peacekeepers serving with the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon were killed in two separate incidents in southern Lebanon within 24 hours on March 29-30, marking the deadliest stretch for the mission since the Israel-Hezbollah conflict reignited on March 2.

items.title: Trump confirms US is negotiating with Iran's Ghalibaf

featured_image.name: Iran's Parliament speaker takes center role in peace talks

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday publicly identified Iranian Parliamentary Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf as the person the United States has been negotiating with to end the war with Iran, telling the New York Post that "we'll find out in about a week" whether Ghalibaf is someone America can work with.[1]

The confirmation ends days of speculation after Trump last week announced on Truth Social that "very good and productive conversations" were taking place between Washington and Tehran without naming his counterpart. Trump had previously described the official only as "a top person" who is "highly respected".[2][3]

items.title: Renoir, Cezanne, Matisse paintings stolen in 3-minute Italian museum heist

featured_image.name: Paintings 'worth millions' stolen from museum in Italy | World News

items.description: Four masked thieves broke into one of Italy's most prestigious private museums on the night of March 22–23 and made off with three masterpieces worth an estimated €9 million (£7.8 million) in a raid that lasted less than three minutes, authorities confirmed on Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Trump weighs sending troops into Iran to seize uranium

featured_image.name: Trump faces his most difficult Iran war decision: Will he deploy ... - PBS

items.description: President Donald Trump is considering a military operation to extract nearly 1,000 pounds of enriched uranium from Iranian nuclear sites, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, a move that would mark a dramatic escalation in a war now entering its fifth week. No final decision has been made, but officials say Trump remains open to the idea, which aligns with his stated goal of ensuring Iran never develops a nuclear weapon.[1][2]
